Policy Name: EC2 instance should use an instance profile
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.18 Ensure IAM instance roles are used for AWS resource access from instances - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to associate an instance profile with an EC2 instance via AWS CLI:    
```
aws ec2 associate-iam-instance-profile --iam-instance-profile Name=<instanceProfileName> --instance-id {{instanceId}}
```

Policy Name: EC2 instance should use IMDSv2
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.6 Ensure that EC2 Metadata Service only allows IMDSv2 - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to configure EC2 to only allow the use of IMDSv2 via AWS CLI:  
```  
aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id {{instanceId}} --http-tokens required --http-endpoint enabled  
```
>**Note**  
>It is recommended to make sure the EC2's software supports IMDSv2 prior to performing this command.  
>Follow [this link](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environments-cfg-ec2-imds.html) for things to take into consideration before switching over to using only IMDSv2, and [this link](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-metadata-transition-to-version-2.html) for tools and recommendations for performing the transition.

	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

	--security-group-rules SecurityGroupRuleId=<SecurityGroupRuleId>,SecurityGroupRule="{FromPort=<FromPort>,ToPort=<ToPort>,IpProtocol=<IpProtocol>,CidrIpv4=<CidrIp>}"

aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

Policy Name: Access keys should be rotated every 90 days
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to remove the outdated active access key pair via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: S3 Bucket policy should deny HTTP requests
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.1.1 Ensure S3 Bucket Policy is set to deny HTTP requests - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to deny HTTP requests to the bucket via AWS CLI:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy \
    --bucket {{bucketName}} \
    --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:*","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::{{bucketName}}/*","Condition":{"Bool":{"aws:SecureTransport":"false"}}}]}'  
```
>**Note**  
For further remediation assistance, see [AWS video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obCm_RMYMp8&ab_channel=AmazonWebServices) on this matter.

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with SSE-KMS
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following to configure CloudTrail to use SSE-KMS:  
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the CloudTrail [console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail).  
2. In the left navigation pane, choose Trails.  
3. Click on a Trail.  
4. Under the S3 section click on the edit button (pencil icon).  
5. Click Advanced.  
6. Select an existing CMK from the KMS key Id drop-down menu.  
7. Click Save.  
8. You will see a notification message stating that you need to have decrypt permissions on the specified KMS key to decrypt log files.  
9. Click Yes.
>**Note**  
>* Ensure the CMK is located in the same region as the S3 bucket.  
>* You will need to apply a KMS Key policy on the selected CMK in order for CloudTrail as a service to encrypt and decrypt log files using the CMK provided. Steps are provided [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) for editing the selected CMK Key policy.
>* Customer created keys incur an additional cost. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/) for more information.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Perform the following command to deny HTTP requests to the bucket via AWS CLI:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy \
    --bucket {{bucketName}} \
    --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:*","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::{{bucketName}}/*","Condition":{"Bool":{"aws:SecureTransport":"false"}}}]}'  
```
>**Note**  
For further remediation assistance, see [AWS video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obCm_RMYMp8&ab_channel=AmazonWebServices) on this matter.

Policy Name: Access keys should not be set up during the initial IAM User setup for all IAM Users that have a console password
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.11 Do not setup access keys during initial user setup for all IAM users that have a console password - Level 1 (Manual)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete the access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:  
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there are two access keys, run the following command twice, one for each key ID.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

Policy Name: EC2 instance should use IMDSv2
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.6 Ensure that EC2 Metadata Service only allows IMDSv2 - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to configure EC2 to only allow the use of IMDSv2 via AWS CLI:  
```  
aws ec2 modify-instance-metadata-options --instance-id {{instanceId}} --http-tokens required --http-endpoint enabled  
```
>**Note**  
>It is recommended to make sure the EC2's software supports IMDSv2 prior to performing this command.  
>Follow [this link](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/environments-cfg-ec2-imds.html) for things to take into consideration before switching over to using only IMDSv2, and [this link](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-metadata-transition-to-version-2.html) for tools and recommendations for performing the transition.

Policy Name: Database instance should not be publicly accessible
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.3 Ensure that public access is not given to RDS Instance - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command in order to disable the publicly accessible configuration of the database instance via AWS CLI:
```  
aws rds modify-db-instance \
	--region {{region}} \
	--db-instance-identifier {{instanceIdentifier}} \
	--no-publicly-accessible
```
**Note**  
If you have a Neptune instance failing this rule - this setting has been deprecated and is not used in newer Neptune versions. It is recommended to upgrade any outdated Neptune Clusters and Instances engine versions.

Policy Name: Database instance automatic minor version upgrade should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.2 Ensure Auto Minor Version Upgrade feature is Enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to enable automatic minor version upgrades for the RDS instance via AWS CLI:
```
aws rds modify-db-instance \
    --region {{region}} \
    --db-instance-identifier {{instanceID}} \
    --auto-minor-version-upgrade \
    [--apply-immediately]
```
The change is applied during the next scheduled maintenance window, unless the `--apply-immediately` parameter is enabled for this request.
**Note**  
For Neptune use the CLI command `aws neptune modify-db-instance` instead.

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

Policy Name: Access keys should be rotated every 90 days
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to remove the outdated active access key pair via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: VPC NACL should not allow unrestricted SSH access
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.1 Ensure no Network ACLs allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to delete or modify the inbound NACL rule(s) to restrict SSH access via AWS CLI:

1. Use the following command to view the current NACL configuration (or view the resource JSON in Wiz):
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls \
--network-acl-ids {{naclId}}
```

If you wish to modify the rule, proceed to step 2a. If you prefer deleting the rule, skip to step 2b. Perform one of the commands for every overly permissive rule found.

2a. To modify an inbound rule, use the rule number from the previous output in the following command, and insert the required port range and IP CIDR:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--protocol tcp \
--rule-action allow \
--rule-number <rule number> \
--ingress \
--cidr-block <IP CIDR> \
--port-range From=<port>,To=<port>
``` 

2b. To delete the overly permissive rule use the rule number from the previous output in the following command:
```
aws ec2 delete-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--ingress \
--rule-number <ruleNumber>  
```

Perform the following commands to delete or modify the inbound NACL rule(s) to restrict RDP access via AWS CLI:

1. Use the following command to view the current NACL configuration (or view the resource JSON in Wiz):
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls \
--network-acl-ids {{naclId}}
```

If you wish to modify the rule, proceed to step 2a. If you prefer deleting the rule, skip to step 2b. Perform one of the commands for every overly permissive rule found.

2a. To modify an inbound rule, use the rule number from the previous output in the following command, and insert the required port range and IP CIDR:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--protocol tcp \
--rule-action allow \
--rule-number <rule number> \
--ingress \
--cidr-block <IP CIDR> \
--port-range From=<port>,To=<port>
``` 

2b. To delete the overly permissive rule use the rule number from the previous output in the following command:
```
aws ec2 delete-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--ingress \
--rule-number <ruleNumber>  
```

1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.

```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```

Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: VPC NACL should not allow unrestricted SSH access
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.1 Ensure no Network ACLs allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to delete or modify the inbound NACL rule(s) to restrict SSH access via AWS CLI:

1. Use the following command to view the current NACL configuration (or view the resource JSON in Wiz):
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls \
--network-acl-ids {{naclId}}
```

If you wish to modify the rule, proceed to step 2a. If you prefer deleting the rule, skip to step 2b. Perform one of the commands for every overly permissive rule found.

2a. To modify an inbound rule, use the rule number from the previous output in the following command, and insert the required port range and IP CIDR:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--protocol tcp \
--rule-action allow \
--rule-number <rule number> \
--ingress \
--cidr-block <IP CIDR> \
--port-range From=<port>,To=<port>
``` 

2b. To delete the overly permissive rule use the rule number from the previous output in the following command:
```
aws ec2 delete-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--ingress \
--rule-number <ruleNumber>  
```

Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to remove the outdated active access key pair via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: VPC NACL should not allow unrestricted RDP access
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.1 Ensure no Network ACLs allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to delete or modify the inbound NACL rule(s) to restrict RDP access via AWS CLI:

1. Use the following command to view the current NACL configuration (or view the resource JSON in Wiz):
```
aws ec2 describe-network-acls \
--network-acl-ids {{naclId}}
```

If you wish to modify the rule, proceed to step 2a. If you prefer deleting the rule, skip to step 2b. Perform one of the commands for every overly permissive rule found.

2a. To modify an inbound rule, use the rule number from the previous output in the following command, and insert the required port range and IP CIDR:
```
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--protocol tcp \
--rule-action allow \
--rule-number <rule number> \
--ingress \
--cidr-block <IP CIDR> \
--port-range From=<port>,To=<port>
``` 

2b. To delete the overly permissive rule use the rule number from the previous output in the following command:
```
aws ec2 delete-network-acl-entry \
--network-acl-id {{naclId}} \
--ingress \
--rule-number <ruleNumber>  
```

Policy Name: Access keys should be rotated every 90 days
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to remove the outdated active access key pair via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: Account should have CloudTrail logging enabled in all regions
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.1 Ensure CloudTrail is enabled in all regions - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to create and configure a CloudTrail to log all management events for the AWS Account via AWS CLI:

**1. Create a multi-region trail:**
```
aws cloudtrail create-trail \
    --name <trailName> \
    --s3-bucket-name <bucketName> \
    --is-multi-region-trail
```

**2. Configure event selectors to capture all management events:**
```
aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors \
    --trail-name <trailName> \
    --event-selectors '[{"ReadWriteType":"All","IncludeManagementEvents":true}]'
```

**3. Start logging:**
```
aws cloudtrail start-logging \
    --name <trailName>
```

**4. Verify the trail is logging:**
```
aws cloudtrail get-trail-status \
    --name <trailName>
```

>**Note**  
After creating, please follow the AWS CloudTrail best practices in this [link.](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/aws-cloudtrail-best-practices/)

Policy Name: IAM User should have only one active access key

Policy Name: IAM User should have only one active access key
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.13 Ensure there is only one active access key available for any single IAM user - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete one of the active access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete one of the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: IAM User should not have any policies attached
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.15 Ensure IAM Users Receive Permissions Only Through Groups - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to detach policies from users via AWS CLI:  
```  
aws iam detach-user-policy \
    --user-name {{userName}} \
    --policy-arn <value>  
```  
Repeat the command for the following policy ARNs:  
```  
{{policies}}  
```  
Once the policies are removed, assign the user to the correct role or group instead. In addition, it is advised to delete any policies that are left unused. You can use the `delete-policy` command to delete any unneeded policies.

Policy Name: Access keys should be rotated every 90 days

Remediation Steps:

1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: Access keys should be rotated every 90 days
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to remove the outdated active access key pair via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: IAM User credentials unused for 45 days or more should be disabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.12 Ensure credentials unused for 45 days or greater are disabled - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to disable access keys, disable console access, or delete the user via AWS CLI:

### Disable access keys  
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:
```
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```
2. Use the following command to disable the access keys.  
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of active access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there is more than one, run the next command twice, once for each Key ID.  
```
aws iam update-access-key \
	--user-name {{userName}} \
	--access-key <value> \
	--status Inactive
```
>**Note**  
Once an access key is disabled, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

### Disable console access  
Use the following command to disable the user's console access:
```
aws iam delete-login-profile \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

### Delete user  
```
aws iam delete-user \
	--user-name {{userName}}
```

Policy Name: S3 Bucket policy should deny HTTP requests
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.1.1 Ensure S3 Bucket Policy is set to deny HTTP requests - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to deny HTTP requests to the bucket via AWS CLI:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy \
    --bucket {{bucketName}} \
    --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:*","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::{{bucketName}}/*","Condition":{"Bool":{"aws:SecureTransport":"false"}}}]}'  
```
>**Note**  
For further remediation assistance, see [AWS video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obCm_RMYMp8&ab_channel=AmazonWebServices) on this matter.

Remediation Steps: This action is not available via AWS CLI. Use the AWS Management Console instead. Follow [this link](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_mfa_enable_virtual.html#enable-virt-mfa-for-root) for the steps to enable MFA for the Root account.

Policy Name: S3 Bucket policy should deny HTTP requests
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.1.1 Ensure S3 Bucket Policy is set to deny HTTP requests - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to deny HTTP requests to the bucket via AWS CLI:
```
aws s3api put-bucket-policy \
    --bucket {{bucketName}} \
    --policy '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Deny","Principal":"*","Action":"s3:*","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::{{bucketName}}/*","Condition":{"Bool":{"aws:SecureTransport":"false"}}}]}'  
```
>**Note**  
For further remediation assistance, see [AWS video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=obCm_RMYMp8&ab_channel=AmazonWebServices) on this matter.

Policy Name: S3 Bucket should have all 'Block Public Access' settings enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.1.4 Ensure that S3 Buckets are configured with 'Block public access (bucket settings)' - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to enable the Block Public Access settings via AWS CLI:  
```  
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket {{bucketName}} --public-access-block-configuration "BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true"  
```

>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

```  
aws iam list-access-keys

```  
aws iam delete-access-key /

```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: Root account access keys should not exist
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.4 Ensure no 'root' user account access key exists - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps, while being signed in as the Root user, in order to delete the root user's access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the Root user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` from the output and paste it into the `access-key-id` value in the next step.  
```  
aws iam list-access-keys  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access key(s).   
```  
aws iam delete-access-key /  
    --access-key-id <value>  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

Policy Name: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with SSE-KMS

Remediation Steps:
Perform the following to configure CloudTrail to use SSE-KMS:

2. In the left navigation pane, choose Trails.  
3. Click on a Trail.  
4. Under the S3 section click on the edit button (pencil icon).  
5. Click Advanced.  
6. Select an existing CMK from the KMS key Id drop-down menu.  
7. Click Save.  
8. You will see a notification message stating that you need to have decrypt permissions on the specified KMS key to decrypt log files.  
9. Click Yes.
>**Note**  
>* Ensure the CMK is located in the same region as the S3 bucket.  
>* You will need to apply a KMS Key policy on the selected CMK in order for CloudTrail as a service to encrypt and decrypt log files using the CMK provided. Steps are provided [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) for editing the selected CMK Key policy.
>* Customer created keys incur an additional cost. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/) for more information.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with SSE-KMS
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following to configure CloudTrail to use SSE-KMS:  
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the CloudTrail [console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail).  
2. In the left navigation pane, choose Trails.  
3. Click on a Trail.  
4. Under the S3 section click on the edit button (pencil icon).  
5. Click Advanced.  
6. Select an existing CMK from the KMS key Id drop-down menu.  
7. Click Save.  
8. You will see a notification message stating that you need to have decrypt permissions on the specified KMS key to decrypt log files.  
9. Click Yes.
>**Note**  
>* Ensure the CMK is located in the same region as the S3 bucket.  
>* You will need to apply a KMS Key policy on the selected CMK in order for CloudTrail as a service to encrypt and decrypt log files using the CMK provided. Steps are provided [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) for editing the selected CMK Key policy.
>* Customer created keys incur an additional cost. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/) for more information.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with SSE-KMS
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following to configure CloudTrail to use SSE-KMS:  
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the CloudTrail [console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail).  
2. In the left navigation pane, choose Trails.  
3. Click on a Trail.  
4. Under the S3 section click on the edit button (pencil icon).  
5. Click Advanced.  
6. Select an existing CMK from the KMS key Id drop-down menu.  
7. Click Save.  
8. You will see a notification message stating that you need to have decrypt permissions on the specified KMS key to decrypt log files.  
9. Click Yes.
>**Note**  
>* Ensure the CMK is located in the same region as the S3 bucket.  
>* You will need to apply a KMS Key policy on the selected CMK in order for CloudTrail as a service to encrypt and decrypt log files using the CMK provided. Steps are provided [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) for editing the selected CMK Key policy.
>* Customer created keys incur an additional cost. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/) for more information.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: IAM User with console access should have MFA enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.10 Ensure multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to create and enable a virtual MFA for the user via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a virtual MFA command.    
In the `outfile` value, enter a file path destination on your machine, including the file name (for example: /home/{{userName}}-qr-code.txt).  
```  
aws iam create-virtual-mfa-device \
--virtual-mfa-device-name {{userName}}-MFADevice \
--outfile <value> \
--bootstrap-method Base32StringSeed  
```  
2. Use the following command to enable the MFA for the user.    
Copy the `SerialNumber` output from the previous step and retrieve the `authentication-codes` values from your MFA device. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/iam/features/mfa/?audit=2019q1) to see the list of AWS-supported virtual MFA applications.  
```   
aws iam enable-mfa-device \
--user-name {{userName}} \
--serial-number <value> \
--authentication-code1 <value> \
--authentication-code2 <value>  
```    
If successful, the command does not produce an output, and the user will be required to use MFA in their next login.

	--user-name {{userName}}  
```

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

```

```

aws iam list-access-keys \

```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

```  
aws iam list-access-keys \

```

	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: Access keys should not be set up during the initial IAM User setup for all IAM Users that have a console password
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.11 Do not setup access keys during initial user setup for all IAM users that have a console password - Level 1 (Manual)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete the access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:  
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there are two access keys, run the following command twice, one for each key ID.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: IAM User with console access should have MFA enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.10 Ensure multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enabled for all IAM users that have a console password - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to create and enable a virtual MFA for the user via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a virtual MFA command.    
In the `outfile` value, enter a file path destination on your machine, including the file name (for example: /home/{{userName}}-qr-code.txt).  
```  
aws iam create-virtual-mfa-device \
--virtual-mfa-device-name {{userName}}-MFADevice \
--outfile <value> \
--bootstrap-method Base32StringSeed  
```  
2. Use the following command to enable the MFA for the user.    
Copy the `SerialNumber` output from the previous step and retrieve the `authentication-codes` values from your MFA device. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/iam/features/mfa/?audit=2019q1) to see the list of AWS-supported virtual MFA applications.  
```   
aws iam enable-mfa-device \
--user-name {{userName}} \
--serial-number <value> \
--authentication-code1 <value> \
--authentication-code2 <value>  
```    
If successful, the command does not produce an output, and the user will be required to use MFA in their next login.

Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.13 Ensure there is only one active access key available for any single IAM user - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete one of the active access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete one of the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: EC2 Security Group should restrict access to remote administration ports
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.2 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated), 5.3 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from ::/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to modify or delete the Security Group rule via AWS CLI:

Use the following command to modify the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rules SecurityGroupRuleId=<SecurityGroupRuleId>,SecurityGroupRule="{FromPort=<FromPort>,ToPort=<ToPort>,IpProtocol=<IpProtocol>,CidrIpv4=<CidrIp>}"  
```

Alternatively, use the following command to delete the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

Policy Name: Database instance automatic minor version upgrade should be enabled

Policy Name: Access keys should not be set up during the initial IAM User setup for all IAM Users that have a console password
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.11 Do not setup access keys during initial user setup for all IAM users that have a console password - Level 1 (Manual)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete the access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:  
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there are two access keys, run the following command twice, one for each key ID.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: Access keys should be rotated every 90 days
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.14 Ensure access keys are rotated every 90 days or less - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to remove the outdated active access key pair via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:    
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output where the status is active and the `CreateDate` is 90 days or greater, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",

    {

      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {

      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with SSE-KMS
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following to configure CloudTrail to use SSE-KMS:  
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the CloudTrail [console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail).  
2. In the left navigation pane, choose Trails.  
3. Click on a Trail.  
4. Under the S3 section click on the edit button (pencil icon).  
5. Click Advanced.  
6. Select an existing CMK from the KMS key Id drop-down menu.  
7. Click Save.  
8. You will see a notification message stating that you need to have decrypt permissions on the specified KMS key to decrypt log files.  
9. Click Yes.
>**Note**  
>* Ensure the CMK is located in the same region as the S3 bucket.  
>* You will need to apply a KMS Key policy on the selected CMK in order for CloudTrail as a service to encrypt and decrypt log files using the CMK provided. Steps are provided [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) for editing the selected CMK Key policy.
>* Customer created keys incur an additional cost. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/) for more information.

Policy Name: Access keys should not be set up during the initial IAM User setup for all IAM Users that have a console password
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 1.11 Do not setup access keys during initial user setup for all IAM users that have a console password - Level 1 (Manual)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete the access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:  
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there are two access keys, run the following command twice, one for each key ID.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: EC2 Security Group should restrict access to remote administration ports
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.2 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated), 5.3 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from ::/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)

Use the following command to modify the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rules SecurityGroupRuleId=<SecurityGroupRuleId>,SecurityGroupRule="{FromPort=<FromPort>,ToPort=<ToPort>,IpProtocol=<IpProtocol>,CidrIpv4=<CidrIp>}"  
```

Alternatively, use the following command to delete the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
