Policy Name: Database instance encryption at rest should be enabled
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 2.3.1 Ensure that encryption-at-rest is enabled for RDS Instances - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands in order to encrypt RDS instance via AWS CLI:  
1. Create a snapshot:  
```  
 aws rds create-db-snapshot \
 	--region <region> \
 	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
 	--db-instance-identifier <DBName>  
```  
2. Find the ID of the AWS default KMS key:  
```  
aws kms list-aliases \
	--region <region> \
	--query 'Aliases[?AliasName==`alias/aws/rds`].TargetKeyId'  
```  
3. Copy the snapshot using the default KMSkeyID returned in the previous stage:   
```  
aws rds copy-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--source-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotName> \
	--target-db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted> \
	--copy-tags \
	--kms-key-id <KMSkeyID>  
```  
4. Restore the DB from the snapshot:  
```  
aws rds restore-db-instance-from-db-snapshot \
	--region <region> \
	--db-instance-identifier <DBNameEncrypted> \
	--db-snapshot-identifier <DBSnapshotNameEncrypted>  
```
>**Note**  
> For encrypting Neptune databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/neptune/latest/userguide/encrypt.html).  
> For encrypting DocumentDB databases click [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/developerguide/encryption-at-rest.html).

aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules \

```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: IAM User should have only one active access key

```

Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: CloudTrail logs should be encrypted with SSE-KMS
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.7 Ensure CloudTrail logs are encrypted at rest using KMS CMKs - Level 2 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following to configure CloudTrail to use SSE-KMS:  
1. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and open the CloudTrail [console](https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudtrail).  
2. In the left navigation pane, choose Trails.  
3. Click on a Trail.  
4. Under the S3 section click on the edit button (pencil icon).  
5. Click Advanced.  
6. Select an existing CMK from the KMS key Id drop-down menu.  
7. Click Save.  
8. You will see a notification message stating that you need to have decrypt permissions on the specified KMS key to decrypt log files.  
9. Click Yes.
>**Note**  
>* Ensure the CMK is located in the same region as the S3 bucket.  
>* You will need to apply a KMS Key policy on the selected CMK in order for CloudTrail as a service to encrypt and decrypt log files using the CMK provided. Steps are provided [here](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/create-kms-key-policy-for-cloudtrail.html) for editing the selected CMK Key policy.
>* Customer created keys incur an additional cost. Click [here](https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/) for more information.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```

Policy Name: EC2 Security Group should restrict access to remote administration ports
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.2 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated), 5.3 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from ::/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to modify or delete the Security Group rule via AWS CLI:

Use the following command to modify the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rules SecurityGroupRuleId=<SecurityGroupRuleId>,SecurityGroupRule="{FromPort=<FromPort>,ToPort=<ToPort>,IpProtocol=<IpProtocol>,CidrIpv4=<CidrIp>}"  
```

Alternatively, use the following command to delete the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.2 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated), 5.3 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from ::/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to modify or delete the Security Group rule via AWS CLI:

Use the following command to modify the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rules SecurityGroupRuleId=<SecurityGroupRuleId>,SecurityGroupRule="{FromPort=<FromPort>,ToPort=<ToPort>,IpProtocol=<IpProtocol>,CidrIpv4=<CidrIp>}"  
```

Alternatively, use the following command to delete the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

Policy Name: EC2 Security Group should restrict access to remote administration ports
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 5.2 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated), 5.3 Ensure no security groups allow ingress from ::/0 to remote server administration ports - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following commands to modify or delete the Security Group rule via AWS CLI:

Use the following command to modify the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 modify-security-group-rules \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rules SecurityGroupRuleId=<SecurityGroupRuleId>,SecurityGroupRule="{FromPort=<FromPort>,ToPort=<ToPort>,IpProtocol=<IpProtocol>,CidrIpv4=<CidrIp>}"  
```

Alternatively, use the following command to delete the non-compliant rule(s):
```
aws ec2 revoke-security-group-ingress \
	--group-id {{groupId}} \
	--security-group-rule-ids <value>
```
>**Note**  
>You can find your rule ID on the Security Group page in the AWS Console or by using the command `describe-security-group-rules` on the AWS CLI.

Remediation Steps:
Perform the following steps to delete the access keys via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to list the access keys of the user:  
```  
aws iam list-access-keys \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
2. Use the following command to delete the user's access keys.    
Copy the `AccessKeyId` output of one of the access keys, and paste the value into the `access-key` parameter. If there are two access keys, run the following command twice, one for each key ID.  
```  
aws iam delete-access-key \
	--access-key <value> \
	--user-name {{userName}}  
```  
>**Note**    
Once an access key is removed, any application using it will not work until a new one is configured for it.

Policy Name: CloudTrail event should be integrated with CloudWatch
Compliance Check Name (Wiz Subcategory): 3.4 Ensure CloudTrail trails are integrated with CloudWatch Logs - Level 1 (Automated)
Remediation Steps:
Perform the following command to integrate CloudTrail events into CloudWatch via AWS CLI:    
1. Use the following command to create a log group:  
```  
aws logs create-log-group --log-group-name <logGroupName>  
```  
2. Use the following command to retrieve the log group ARN, you should use it in step 7:  
```  
aws logs describe-log-groups  
```  
3. Create the JSON file that will contain the policy document, open a text editor and save the following policy contents in a file called assume_role_policy_document.json:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
      "Sid": "",  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Principal": {  
        "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"  
      },  
      "Action": "sts:AssumeRole"  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
4. Use the following command to create a role for CloudTrail that enables it to send events to the CloudWatch Logs log group:  
```  
aws iam create-role --role-name <roleName> --assume-role-policy-document file://<assumeRolePath>.json  
```  
5. Create the following role policy document for CloudTrail to grant CloudTrail the permissions required to create a CloudWatch Logs log stream in the log group you specify, and to deliver CloudTrail events to that log stream:  
```  
{  
  "Version": "2012-10-17",  
  "Statement": [  
    {  
  
      "Sid": <createLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:CreateLogStream"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
  
    },  
    {  
      "Sid": <putLogStreamSid>,  
      "Effect": "Allow",  
      "Action": [  
        "logs:PutLogEvents"  
      ],  
      "Resource": [  
        "arn:aws:logs:{{region}}:<accountId>:log-group:<logGroupName>:log-stream:<accountId>_CloudTrail_{{region}}*"  
      ]  
    }  
  ]  
}  
```  
6. Use the following command to apply the policy to the role:  
```  
aws iam put-role-policy --role-name <roleName> --policy-name <policyName> --policy-document file://<rolePolicyDocument>.json  
```  
7. Use the following command to update the trail with the log group and role information:  
```  
aws cloudtrail update-trail --name <logGroupName> --cloud-watch-logs-log-group-arn <logGroupArn> --cloud-watch-logs-role-arn <roleArn>  
```
